title: Principles six to nine
hookLine: prophecy, Moses' unique prophecy, the Torah from heaven, and its permanence

cards: Two verses from the Torah. One: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one." The other is from a list of names in Genesis: the sons of Ham were Cush, and Mizraim, and Put, and Canaan.
One you met yesterday, at the heart of Jewish prayer. The other is easy to skim. Is one of them holier than the other?
Maimonides gives a blunt answer, and it sits at the center of today's four foundations: the ones about prophecy, and about the Torah itself.

teach.b: Principles six to nine. The sixth: prophecy is real. God can speak to human beings, and some people, prepared and open, have heard.
The seventh: the prophecy of Moses stands apart from every other. The Torah itself says so.
In Numbers, God says that with other prophets He speaks in visions and dreams, but with Moses mouth to mouth, plainly, not in riddles.

And at the end of Deuteronomy: no prophet has arisen since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face. That's why the line from last week's saying, from Moses to Moses, carried such weight.
The eighth: the Torah is from heaven. The whole Torah we have, Maimonides says, is the one given to Moses. And here is his blunt answer to the two verses.
There is no difference, he says, between the sons of Ham and Hear, O Israel.

teach.h: EVERY VERSE FROM THE SAME SOURCE.
teach.b: Both come from the same source. Holiness isn't measured by how moving a verse sounds. The ninth: the Torah won't be replaced.
Nothing will be added to it, and nothing taken away. Deuteronomy says it directly: "thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it." Put the four together and you get a chain.
God speaks. Moses hears most clearly. What he receives is the Torah.
And the Torah stays. Jews today hold the eighth and ninth in different ways, and that difference gets a day of its own soon.

how: The Torah is read aloud from a handwritten scroll in the synagogue on Shabbat, Mondays, Thursdays and festivals, and read through in order, over a yearly cycle or, in some communities, a longer one.

games.q: what does “principles six to nine” mean?
o: prophecy, Moses' prophecy, and a Torah from heaven
four rules for telling a true prophet from a false
the four books of the prophets after the Torah

games.q: principles six to nine — tap the pairs.

s: Maimonides treats a list of names as less holy than the Shema
he says there is no difference between the sons of Ham and Hear, O Israel.
the Torah itself says Moses' prophecy is unlike others'
Numbers says God spoke with him mouth to mouth, and Deuteronomy says no prophet like him arose.
the ninth principle says the Torah will be replaced someday
it says the Torah won't be replaced: nothing added, nothing taken away.

games.q: you're Maimonides. someone asks: which came from heaven, "Hear, O Israel" or a list of the sons of Ham?
games.why: he says there is no difference between them: the whole Torah comes from the same source.

practice: Bring to mind the words that guide you most, from scripture, a parent or a teacher, and ask quietly where they reached you from. Follow the chain back, one link at a time, as far as you can. Then set the question down.

wordCard.voice: Principles six to nine. Prophecy is real, Moses' prophecy stands apart, the Torah is from heaven, and the Torah will not be replaced. Today's word.
